Q97760438.label: Movement for the Organization of the Country
Q97760438.wiki: Movement for the Organization of the Country
Q97760438.summary: The Movement for the Organization of the Country is a political party in Haiti, founded by Daniel Fignolé in 1946 as the Peasant Worker Movement.

Q5052598.label: Catherine Connolly
Q5052598.summary: Catherine Martina Ann Connolly is an Irish politician serving as the president of Ireland since 11 November 2025. She had been a Teachta Dála (TD) for the Galway West constituency from 2016 until her election as president in 2025.

Q18058934.label: 2015 Dutch Senate election
Q18058934.summary: Elections of the Dutch Senate were held on 26 May 2015. The elected senators were sworn in on 9 June 2015.

Q699574.label: 1961 West German federal election
Q699574.summary: A federal election was held in West Germany on 17 September 1961 to elect the members of the fourth Bundestag. The CDU/CSU remained the largest faction, winning 242 of the 499 seats. However, the loss of its majority and the All-German Party losing all its seats led to the CDU having to negotiate a coalition with the long-term junior coalition partner, the Free Democratic Party, leading to a demand for long-term chancellor Konrad Adenauer to leave office in 1963, halfway through his term.

mentions.c: West Germany / Germany: 1961 West German federal election

Q680630.label: 1979 Austrian legislative election
Q680630.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 6 May 1979. The Socialist Party won a fourth consecutive term in government, and its third as a majority government, winning 95 of 183 seats. Voter turnout was 92.2%. As of the 2024 election, the Socialist Party's result is the most seats that an Austrian party has won in a free election, as well as the last time that an Austrian political party has won an outright majority at the federal level.

Q28341942.label: 2017 Hungarian presidential election
Q28341942.summary: An indirect presidential election was held in Hungary on 13 March 2017. Incumbent President János Áder was re-elected with an absolute majority for a second term.

Q4996278.label: 1953 Bulgarian parliamentary election
Q4996278.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria on 20 December 1953. Voters were presented with a single list from the Fatherland Front, dominated by the Bulgarian Communist Party. As the Fatherland Front was the only organisation to contest the election and all candidate lists had to be approved by the Front, voters only had the option of voting for or against the Front list. Only 0.2% of vote were cast against the Front. Voter turnout was reportedly 99.5%.

Q223414.label: Octavian Goga
Q223414.summary: Octavian Goga was a Romanian far-right politician, poet, and writer who served as Prime Minister of Romania.

Q991414.label: Estonian People's Party
Q991414.summary: The Estonian People's Party was a centre-right political party in Estonia.

Q4832438.label: 1992 Azerbaijani presidential election
Q4832438.summary: Presidential elections were held in Azerbaijan on 7 June 1992. The elections were the first in Azerbaijan in more than seventy years not held under communist control and featured the unprecedented use of television, posters, and other media by multiple candidates to communicate platforms and solicit votes.

Q130314422.label: 2024 Lebanon electronic device attacks
Q130314422.desc: explosive device attacks in Lebanon and Syria
Q130314422.summary: On 17 and 18 September 2024, thousands of handheld pagers and hundreds of walkie-talkies intended for use by Hezbollah exploded simultaneously in two separate events across Lebanon and Syria, in an Israeli attack nicknamed Operation Grim Beeper.

Q7508662.label: Battle of Sidi Barrani
Q7508662.desc: battle in Egypt 10-11 December 1940 during World War II
Q7508662.summary: The Battle of Sidi Barrani (10–11 December 1940) was the opening battle of Operation Compass, the first big British attack of the Western Desert Campaign of the Second World War. Sidi Barrani, on the Mediterranean coast in Egypt, had been occupied by the Italian 10th Army, during the Italian invasion of Egypt (9–16 September 1940) and was attacked by British, Commonwealth and imperial troops, who re-captured the port.

Q85985974.label: Battle of Chongju
Q85985974.summary: The Battle of Chongju, also spelled Battle of Jeongju took place during the United Nations Command (UN) offensive towards the Yalu River, which followed the North Korean invasion of South Korea at the start of the Korean War. The battle was fought between Australian forces from 3rd Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment and the 17th Tank Brigade of the Korean People's Army (KPA) for control of Chongju, North Korea and the surrounding area.

Q7097526.label: Operation Sealords
Q7097526.desc: military operation during the Vietnam War
Q7097526.summary: Operation Sealords was a military operation that took place during the Vietnam War.

Q7097014.label: Operation Eagle
Q7097014.summary: Operation Eagle was a Sri Lanka Air Force operation to resupply and rescue critically wounded service personnel from the old Dutch Fort of Jaffna held by the Sri Lanka Army and besieged by the LTTE on July 3, 1990. The successful rescue operation gained headlines, leading to much rejoicing island-wide and helped increase morale.

mentions.c: Part of Sri Lankan Civil War

Q17015478.label: Battle of Al-Malihah
Q17015478.summary: The Battle of Al-Malihah took place in the Rif Dimashq Governorate during the Syrian Civil War.

Q747702.label: Higgs mechanism
Q747702.desc: mechanism in quantum field theory in which spontaneous symmetry breaking causes gauge bosons to acquire mass
Q747702.summary: In the Standard Model of particle physics, the Higgs mechanism is essential to explain the generation mechanism of the property "mass" for gauge bosons. Without the Higgs mechanism, all bosons (one of the two classes of particles, the other being fermions) would be considered massless, but measurements show that the W+, W−, and Z0 bosons actually have relatively large masses of around 80 GeV/c2 (in comparison to other particles like protons and neutrons, at about 1 GeV/c2). The Higgs field resolves this conundrum.

Q472246.label: Machiavellianism
Q472246.desc: political philosophy named after and posed by Niccolò Machiavelli
Q472246.summary: Machiavellianism is widely defined as the political philosophy of the Italian Renaissance diplomat Niccolò Machiavelli, usually associated with realism in foreign and domestic politics, and with the view that those who lead governments must prioritize the stability of the regime over ethical concerns. There is no scholarly consensus as to the precise nature of Machiavelli's philosophy, or what his intentions were with his works. The word Machiavellianism first appeared in the English language in 1607, due to Machiavelli's popularity, often as a byword for unsavory government politics.
